title: silene cucubalus subsp. prostrata
intro: Silene cucubalus subsp. prostrata, commonly known as the creeping sweet violet or creeping wild pansy, is a sub-species of the Silene cucubalus plant, which is native to Europe and Asia. This plant has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, particularly in reducing inflammation and alleviating respiratory issues such as bronchitis and coughs. The health benefits of Silene cucubalus subsp. prostrata include its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, which contribute to its therapeutic actions, such as reducing fever and treating skin conditions. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, saponins, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and health benefits.
